national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will interact with participants of Seva Yatra today via video conference, who are travelling from Varanasi in UP to Vadnagar in Gujarat under Seva Sankalp Abhiyan. The interaction with the Prime Minister will give the Seva Yatris a chance to share their experiences from the journey, which is intended to connect youth participation and community service across the locations covered by the teams. The Seva Yatra began on September 17 and is part of the wider ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’ to highlight PM Modi’s 25 years of public life. The participants are travelling through towns, districts, talukas and villages, with the programme focusing on taking community service and public engagement activities to the grassroots. The journey is not limited to a motorcycle expedition but is designed to bring together service, communication, youth participation, social welfare, cultural connect and community mobilisation at different locations along the route. The two-way motorcycle yatras between Varanasi and Vadnagar involve young participants travelling across multiple states, districts and villages. During the journey, the Seva Yatris have engaged with local communities and participated in service-oriented activities. These include cleanliness drives and interactions with beneficiaries and residents, as well as activities at schools, hospitals, nursing homes, and other community locations. The journey is scheduled to continue until October 7. The Prime Minister yesterday interacted with participants of the Seva Yatra, travelling from Vadnagar to Varanasi and praised their ongoing journey as a significant step toward grassroots nation-building. During the interaction, Mr Modi asked the participants about their experiences on the road, their interactions with people and the new learnings they had gathered during the journey. Drawing from his own organisational background within the party, Mr Modi acknowledged the hardships participants face, including shifting weather conditions and changing locations. During the interaction, the Prime Minister connected with the travellers’ current experiences, noting that such cross-country yatras play a vital role in helping the younger generation understand the country’s diversity. The interaction placed emphasis on the idea that a yatra is not merely about travelling from one place to another, but about meeting people, understanding communities and translating the spirit of seva into action. The Prime Minister also connected the ongoing efforts of the Seva Yatris with the larger journey of nation-building towards Viksit Bharat 2047, highlighting the role of young people in taking this spirit of service to the grassroots.

national_raw_news.title: 15 mins ago | National 12 Make in India initiative completes 12 years
national_raw_news.content: Today marks 12 years of Make in India. It was on this day in 2014 that the initiative was launched with the ambition of becoming a global hub for manufacturing, design and innovation. The initiative has transformed India’s manufacturing landscape by expanding production, investment and capabilities across industries. Akashvani correspondent reports that over the years, Make in India has opened new opportunities for businesses and investors to participate in India’s manufacturing journey. The initiative has subsequently been expanded under Make in India 2.0. The initiative now focuses on 27 sectors, which include 15 in manufacturing and 12 in services. The initiative focused on facilitating investment, fostering innovation and developing world-class infrastructure. Guided by ‘Minimum Government, Maximum Governance’, it has also sought to modernise processes and policies. Under the initiative, India’s electronics production increased nearly sevenfold, from 1.9 lakh crore rupees in 2014-15 to over 13 lakh crore in 2025-26. Mobile-phone production rose approximately 33-fold, from 18 thousand crore to 6.27 lakh crore over the same period. During this period, Indian Railways manufactured nearly 55 thousand coaches over 2014-24, while average annual railway coach production rose from less than 3 thousand 300 during 2004-14 to over 5 thousand during 2014-24. Over 6 thousand 6 hundred Linke Hofmann Busch (LHB) coaches were manufactured in 2025-26. Further, under the Make in India initiative, the country’s indigenous defence production increased from 46 thousand 429 crore in 2014-15 to a record 1.78 lakh crore in Financial Year 2025-26, bringing production to nearly four times its 2014-15 level. The initiative now goes beyond producing more goods and focuses on building the skills, technology and capacity needed to make them in India.

national_raw_news.title: 31 mins ago | Regional News 52 4th edition of UP International Trade Show to begin in Greater Noida
national_raw_news.content: The fourth edition of the UP International Trade Show (UPITS) will begin today at the India Expo Centre and Mart in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh. Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will inaugurate the five-day event. The exhibition, themed ‘Ultimate Sourcing Begins Here’, will run until September 29th, connecting the state’s entrepreneurs, manufacturers and exporters directly with the global market. Briefing the media, Uttar Pradesh MSME Minister Bhupendra Chaudhary highlighted the objective of establishing Uttar Pradesh as a global sourcing hub. He said the state is home to over 96 lakh MSME units and stated that UPITS will provide them with new opportunities for market expansion, investment, exports and employment. Akashvani correspondent reports that the event is expected to witness participation of over 2,400 exhibitors, 1.5 lakh B2B buyers and more than 4.5 lakh general visitors. Over 550 international buyers from 85 countries are also expected to attend the event. Partner countries for this edition include Austria, Japan, Russia, Singapore, Belarus and Vietnam. Additionally, reflecting the prominent role of women in trade and industry, around 300 women representatives will actively participate in the event. The exhibition will showcase various industries and sectors, including agriculture, automobiles, defence, IT, health, tourism and renewable energy. A major highlight this year is the introduction of the ‘One District, One Cuisine’ initiative, which will be featured alongside the ‘One District, One Product’ scheme to present the state’s traditional culinary heritage to the world. Buyers and exhibitors can pre-schedule their B2B meetings through a dedicated UPITS app. The event will also feature knowledge sessions, fashion shows and cultural programmes.
